title: Counter
blurb: The smallest real contract: one number in storage, a view that reads it, two changes that move it, an owner-only reset, and a log line per change. Every NEAR contract is this shape, just bigger.
steps: Press Build: cargo compiles src/lib.rs to a .wasm file.
Press Test: the unit tests run in a fake NEAR runtime, no chain needed.
Press Ship: the .wasm lands on your testnet account (the account IS the contract).
Open the CALL tab: VIEW get, then CHANGE increment, then VIEW get again.

walkthrough.say: This struct IS the contract's storage. NEAR serializes it with borsh and keeps it under the account. Whatever fields you put here persist between calls.
The constructor. It runs once, in the same transaction as the deploy if you batch it (the workshop does). After that, calling it again fails: state already exists.
&self = a VIEW method. Free to call, no key, no gas for the caller, cannot change storage. The CALL tab's VIEW mode talks to these.
&mut self = a CHANGE method. Needs a signed transaction and gas. The SDK writes the new state back when the method returns.
Who is calling. On NEAR this is the account that sent the call, which is how a contract knows its owner. There is no msg.sender; this is it.
The contract's way of saying no. If the condition is false the whole call reverts and the message becomes the error the caller sees.
An event on NEAR is just a log line with this prefix (NEP-297). Indexers and the TX tab pick it up. Nothing is stored; it is a receipt.
Unit tests build a fake runtime: you choose who the caller is and what they attached, then call the methods like plain Rust. Runs in a second, no chain.
